name: loading
description: A composed loading-placeholder pattern for lists, cards, and stacks. Skeleton is the atom; Loading is the canonical molecule most surfaces want.

props.name: variant
props.description: Layout family — picks the row shape.

props.name: rows
props.description: Number of placeholder rows to render. Each row may contain multiple Skeleton elements depending on variant — list emits 1 per row; card emits 3 (heading + 2 body lines); stack emits 3 (avatar + 2 text lines).

props.name: label
props.description: sr-only label announced by screen readers via aria-live polite.

variants.name: variant
variants.description: Layout family for the placeholder rows.

values.description: Single full-width line per row — table / list / sidebar nav loaders.
values.useWhen: the surface being filled is a flat list of equally-shaped rows

values.description: Heading + two body lines inside a bordered card surface.
values.useWhen: loading a Card-shaped widget (settings panel, dashboard tile)

values.description: Avatar + two-line text block per row — message / contact / search-result loaders.
values.useWhen: loading a list of avatar-paired items (chat history, contact list, comment thread)

examples.title: List loader
examples.description: 5 placeholder rows for a dashboard table

examples.title: Card loader
examples.description: Card-shaped placeholder with heading + 2 body lines

ai.whenToUse: Use when fetching data for a list, card, or avatar-paired stack and you want pre-arranged placeholders. Pair the rows count with how many items you expect — avoid 10-row loaders for 2-item results (jarring on resolve).
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use for a single shaped placeholder (use Skeleton). Don't use when the wait has a measurable percent-done (use Progress). Don't use for full-page transitions where a top progress bar is more informative.
commonMistakes: Forgetting `aria-live` would prevent screen-reader announcement — Loading already wires it; don't override role
Using too many rows — flashes a heavy 'something's wrong' impression
Applying Loading inside a Card AND also wrapping in another Card — double-bordered shimmer

antiPatterns.mistake: Using Loading for a single shaped placeholder (avatar circle, heading line, image rectangle)
antiPatterns.why: Skeleton is the atom; render exactly one Skeleton with the right size class. Loading composes Skeletons for canonical multi-row patterns — no value if you only need one shape.

antiPatterns.mistake: Using Loading when the wait has a measurable percent (file upload, batch import)
antiPatterns.why: Progress's `value` prop announces actual completion to assistive tech. Loading is for indeterminate waits.

antiPatterns.mistake: Using Loading for a full-page route transition where the user just clicked a link
antiPatterns.why: Compose page-shaped Skeletons via `generateStaticParams` + Suspense; full-page Loading flashes 'work is happening here' while the right answer is 'show the page shell instantly.'

ai.accessibilityNotes: role='status' + aria-live='polite' + sr-only label, so screen readers announce on first render. Caller doesn't need to wire any of this.
